clues: This city hugs the south-east shore of an island in the vast Pacific. It is one port in a long chain of islands across that sea.
This island town stays warm all year, yet its summer is mostly dry. A rain shadow steals much of the rain that should fall here.
In 1845, a king moved his realm's capital to this port town. Later kings built it up with palaces and a great church.
Waikiki, the famed beach strip by this town, draws crowds from far away. Its hotels, in rows by the sand, form the heart of the isles' tourist trade.
Hawaii's governor and lawmakers do the state's work in this city. It has been the seat of rule for these islands since 1845.
